name.text: Household Appliance Survey: Calculating Probabilities of Electric Devices

questiontext.text:
A survey is made to determine the number of households having electric appliances in a certain city. It is found that \({@r@} \%\) have radios \((\textbf{R})\), \({@iron@} \%\) have irons \((\textbf{I})\), \({@t@} \%\) have electric toasters \((\textbf{T})\), \({@ir@} \%\) have irons and radio \((\textbf{IR})\), \({@it@} \%\) have irons and electric toasters \((\textbf{IR})\), \({@rt@} \%\) have radio and electric toasters \((\textbf{RT})\) and \({@irt@} \%\) have all three.

Find the probability that a household has at least one of the appliances

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the probability that each household has at least one of the appliances (radio, iron, or electric toaster), we can use the complementary probability and proceed as shown below.

The probability that a household has at least one of the appliances

\(P[R \cup I \cup T]=P[R]+P[I]+P[T]-P[R \cap I]-P[R \cap T]-P[I \cap T]+P[R \cap T\cap I]\)

\(P[R \cup I \cup T]={@float(r/100)@}+{@float(iron/100)@}+{@float(t/100)@}-{@float(ir/100)@}-{@float(rt/100)@}-{@float(it/100)@}+{@float(irt/100)@}={@ta1@}\)
